summary: The narrator, a nineteen-year-old on a bike, is stopped by police while heading home at night. She shows her state photo ID, which she got at nineteen because the curfew for fourteen-year-olds is an hour earlier, and the officers give her five minutes to get home or face juvenile supervision and a fine for her aunt. She recalls the Talk her guardian Monica gave her about how to act around police, and her fear that a records check could link her to an alleged terrorist relative. The excerpt ends with her relief at not being arrested or detained, and a reference to her brother's arrest and the Group.
one_line: A nineteen-year-old Black girl is stopped by police on a curfew night, shows her ID, and is warned to get home.
key_facts: The narrator is nineteen and attends Horizons Technical Academy, which she names to the officer as her school.
The narrator says she is nineteen because lying would lead police to check and she would be busted.
The curfew law applied to anyone under eighteen, at least for kids with brown skin in neighborhoods with a high color-coded arrest rate.
The narrator got a state photo ID as soon as she turned nineteen because the curfew for fourteen is an hour earlier.
The narrator kept her state photo ID tucked in the back of her phone case.
The narrator feared the officer would punch her name into his laptop and find a link to an alleged terrorist relative.
Monica gave the narrator the Talk soon after she went to live with her.
The Talk, as the narrator describes it for Black children, means being told to act respectful and submissive when stopped by cops because they are allowed to kill you if you don't.
The officer told the narrator she had five minutes to get home.
The officer warned that if police saw her one minute later, she would be taken to juvenile supervision and her aunt would get a serious fine.
This was the first time the narrator had been stopped by police since her brother was arrested.
After her brother's arrest, the narrator began harnessing the skills of the Group and her friends to rescue him.
The narrator hiked the last two blocks home after being released, shaking with fear and fury.
Once she reached the top of the steps, her adrenaline rush had turned into a giddy sense of relief.
